conclusions: Confirmed diameter-enumeration defect for duplicate or near-duplicate adjacent polygon vertices: the strict cross-area advance stops on the almost-flat support plateau, and the checked j/j+1 pairs omit the true farthest pair.

For the worst polygon, cyclic rotation alone changes the calipers answer. Removing the adjacent near-duplicate restores the independent distance; reinserting an exact duplicate reproduces underestimation. These are diagnostic copies only, not a proposed production patch.

All 213 saved candidate worst-of-15 values and the lambda=0.2 ranking winner remain unchanged to numerical tolerance. Errors occur in non-maximal scenarios; this is not evidence that diameter() is reliable on arbitrary future polygons.
The completed Q2 continuous-envelope and source-grid evaluations used all-vertex pairwise distances, not rotating calipers. Their numerical-envelope limitations remain unchanged.
MEC is a separate implementation and was not modified or audited by this diagnosis. No failure of a clearance certificate is established here.

The initial reconnaissance recomputed 3195 audit scenarios. This evidence pass reconstructs them and additionally recomputes original numpy-angle scenarios only when their report float differs. Neither pass runs a solver or simulator.
